pr_metadata.title: test(acl): Fix flaky ACL tests with long-running Lua scripts
pr_metadata.description:
- Removed `@pytest.mark.skip("Non deterministic")`
- Lowered number of keys

gold_comments.evidence_requirement: The test sets kostas with `+@string +@scripting` but no key permissions (`~*` missing), yet expects `NOPERM` on key access during script execution — this mismatch causes incorrect test behavior.
gold_comments.rationale: Without `~*` in kostas's ACL, the script cannot access keys, so the `NOPERM` error is expected, but the test's assertion and logic assume the script ran successfully before user deletion — the semantics changed after `acl keys` support was added.
gold_comments._reviewer_comment_full:
The reason that we are getting `NOPERM` now instead of `ConnectionError` is because by the time we disabled the test we added support for `acl keys`. So even if we enabled the test, its semantics got changed because of the new feature. To get it back we need to add `~*` in the acl list of the user `kostas`:

```
//notice the addition of ~* at the end of the acl list
await client.execute_command("ACL SETUSER kostas ON >kk +@string +@scripting ~*")
```

So now we delete a user while they are running a command! 

The second problem with this test, is the `load`. It's really slow. So I suggest to edit the script above and iterate less times: `for i = 1, 1000 do`. This will also require an `await async.sleep(2)` before the assertion below to give time for the script to execute.
